policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere/ketiv differ only in the spelling of the 3ms suffix on the plural (plene סביבתיו vs defective סביבתו); ASV 'round about him' renders either identically and the verse's only note is alternative_rendering on 'barricade', which cannot decide a reading. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
Qere מראשתיו vs ketiv מראשתו is a plene/defective spelling of the same suffixed noun; ASV 'at his head' does not distinguish them and no note is mapped. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

Qere מראשתיו vs ketiv מראשתו is a plene/defective spelling of the same suffixed noun; ASV 'at his head' does not distinguish them, and the verse's only note (hebrew_gloss on 'sons of death') is unrelated. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV text 'Behold the spear, O king!' treats המלך as a vocative, which requires the articular ketiv החנית (an articled noun cannot stand in construct); the qere חנית המלך is the construct 'the king's spear', which ASV relegates to the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, the king's spear'. ASV wording plus the note select the ketiv.
